No valid providers in the chain is kind of what I was expecting to see - the provider which was crashing was last in the chain.

The provider which is supposed to pick up the AWS_PROFILE is near the start.

One thing you could try is setting the env var `AWS_SDK_LOAD_CONFIG` to `1`. This shouldn't be needed as I'm setting the equivalent of this internally, but it is worth a shot.

I tried setting aws.Config.CredentialsChainVerboseErrors - can you give this a go. It might tell us something interesting!

[v1.56.0-beta.5423.6defd328b.fix-s3-sso-crash](https://beta.rclone.org/branch/fix-s3-sso-crash/v1.56.0-beta.5423.6defd328b.fix-s3-sso-crash/) on branch [fix-s3-sso-crash](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/tree/fix-s3-sso-crash) (uploaded in 15-30 mins)

The bit of code which is causing the crash is this

https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/f8884a720006403e0144c9f9a5e898877498340a/backend/s3/s3.go#L1515-L1518

As far as I can see this can never have worked because it doesn't initialise the [tokenFetcher](https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/blob/64c99482708d9bab0281216769f110ae046049fc/aws/credentials/stscreds/web_identity_provider.go#L49-L73
) - that is why we get a `nil` pointer crash

The proper way to initialise this is with the [NewWebIdentityCredentials](https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/blob/64c99482708d9bab0281216769f110ae046049fc/aws/credentials/stscreds/web_identity_provider.go#L77) but I have no idea where to get the other parameters from `roleARN, roleSessionName, path`

This code was originally added in 15d19131bd by @tennix - do you have any ideas on how to fix this?

I'm guessing it has something to do with how the authentication is setup to access this bucket, it uses a role-arn coupled to an external AWS account. This is how the credentials file looks like:

```
[internal]
aws_access_key_id = xxxxxx
aws_secret_access_key = xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

[default]
role_arn=arn:aws:iam::123457891011:role/ExternalRole-out
source_profile=internal
```

And the credentials work, because doing `aws s3 ls s3://somebucket` gives the expected output. 

Some of you have any clue on what could be wrong?
